replacements.Persistir crea copias; revocar exige cor: Persistence creates copies; revocation must cut every path
replacements.Este modelo separa la fila de memoria or: This model separates the original memory row from its derivatives. A future query can retrieve a copy after the turn that created it has ended, and deleting only the source does not guarantee that the influence is gone.
replacements.Propagación de una señal persistida y su: Propagation and revocation of a persisted signal
replacements.Una entrada crea una fila de memoria y d: An input creates a memory row plus index and summary derivatives. A future query can carry those derivatives into a decision and a tool. Revoking only the original row leaves residual paths; invalidating the derivatives cuts them.
replacements.Contraejemplo: eliminar la fila de memor: Counterexample: deleting the memory row while retaining the index or a derived summary leaves a retrieval path. Revocation is complete only when those derivatives are no longer reachable and a regression confirms that the signal does not reappear.
replacements.La señal todavía no persiste: The signal is not persistent yet
replacements.El final del turno elimina el contexto v: The end of the turn removes the visible context. There is no retrievable copy yet.
replacements.El origen desapareció, pero quedan deriv: The source is gone, but derivatives remain
replacements.El índice o el resumen siguen siendo rec: The index or summary remains retrievable. Deleting the original row does not prove forgetting.
replacements.Una consulta futura reabre la ruta: A future query reopens the path
replacements.El derivado recuperado vuelve al context: The retrieved derivative returns to context and can influence a decision that reaches a tool.
replacements.La señal ya tiene una fila de memoria y: The signal now has a memory row and derived representations that can outlive the turn.
replacements.La ruta de recuperación se cerró. Falta: The retrieval path is closed. The result still needs to be confirmed with a regression.
